hero.title: Waddimi Saint-Louis
hero.subtitle: System Engineer | Full Stack Developer
hero.summary: I build scalable systems, robust APIs, and high-impact interfaces for companies that need real results. 5 years delivering fullstack solutions in production, with expertise in technical leadership, cloud architecture, and web/mobile development.

start.title: How it started
paragraphs: My path into programming began in 2017, when I enrolled at Universidad Tecnológica de Santiago (UTESA) to study Systems Engineering. That is where I wrote my first lines of code and realized this was for me, understanding how things work under the hood and building them from scratch.

My first language was C#. It taught me the fundamentals I still rely on today: types, data structures, object-oriented design, and the discipline of writing code someone else can read. Then came JavaScript, and with it the web: suddenly I could build something, open it in a browser, and put it in anyone's hands.

In November 2020, while still studying, I started working as a freelance web developer on platforms like Upwork and Workana. That was two and a half years of turning designs into working sites, wiring front-end to back-end, and learning to work with real clients. That combination — the solid grounding of C# and the reach of JavaScript — shaped the rest of my career, and it is why I work comfortably on both sides of the stack today.

academy.title: Alterna Academy and finding a mentor
paragraphs: In 2022 I joined Alterna Academy, a programming school that marked a clear before and after. University gave me the theory and freelancing gave me the craft, the academy taught me how real software gets built as a team, with the practices and pace the industry demands.

That is where I met Eduardo Burgos, a software engineer with more than 20 years in the field and CEO of Alterna Academy. He was my mentor, he is someone I look up to, and today he is also a good friend. Much of how I think about development — making technical decisions with judgment, reviewing code honestly, teaching whoever comes next — comes straight from him.

Shortly after, in April 2023, I joined ProDoctivity SRL as a fullstack developer: my first formal role inside a product team, working with React, TypeScript, Node, Docker, and microservices. I graduated from UTESA in 2024, and since then I have kept adding projects at IMarket and Higher Bit Solutions, where I also took on technical leadership.

utesa.title: Giving back at UTESA
paragraphs: I had the honor of taking part in a tech event at Universidad Tecnológica de Santiago (UTESA), where I spoke about how to land your first job in tech, what a developer's day-to-day actually looks like, and a bit about my own path.
As a graduate of both UTESA and Alterna Academy, being able to share my experience and learning with people starting their careers in tech meant a lot to me.

All of it was possible thanks to Juan José Días Nerio, director of the Software Engineering program at UTESA and one of my great teachers, whose support and vision made the experience genuinely rewarding.
I shared the stage with outstanding professionals, and it was incredible to see the passion and experience each of them brought.

today.title: Why I do it
paragraphs: Events like that one remind me why I love what I do, and how much it matters to share knowledge, inspire, and connect with other professionals. It was a rewarding experience I would gladly repeat.
I still work with the same idea I started with: build things that genuinely work, learn from people who know more than I do, and give back some of what I received to those just getting started.
